description: The Jawz Dashboard: where the world stands, in six readings. Regime (GREEN / YELLOW / RED: consumer mood and money together), Money (PLENTIFUL / STEADY / SCARCER: the Fed, ECB, Bank of Japan and PBoC balance sheets in dollars), Business cycle (SPRING / SUMMER / FALL / WINTER: growth, a vote of factory output, jobs and investment, crossed with prices), Financial conditions (LOOSE / EASING / NEUTRAL / TIGHTENING / TIGHT: rates and credit), Store of value (RISING / MIXED / FALLING: gold and bitcoin) and Investment (BOOMING / STEADY / FADING: the AI build-out, from data centres, chips, the four big builders' capital spending and power). Each card carries its rule in one sentence, the badge with the date it has held since, the badge's last three prints, and the rows behind it, each with its last three prints (date, word and value as the card writes it) and a data-quality status (ok, stale or unavailable). The summary has the six badges, what set each, and the biggest risk in one line. Returned three ways: the dashboard object as structured content, a short card as markdown text (one line per reading with what set it and since when, the biggest risk, and the link to the full dashboard), and the full card as a PNG image. as_of (YYYY-MM-DD, optional) returns the dashboard as Jawz would have read it that day, using only data published by then, with today's rules applied: rules_note says so and, when Jawz's daily snapshot for that date is on file, what Jawz published that day. as_of reaches back 365 days and excludes today, which is the default; a future date or one before the window returns an error stating the supported range. In a dated read every row carries point_in_time. The Investment card's Data centres and Chips rows are not point in time (the Census tables behind them keep only their revised figures, so a dated read shows those months as revised since) and point_in_time_note names them; every other row is as published by that date. The detail behind the cards is in get_macro_regime, get_financial_conditions, get_growth_indicators and get_inflation_indicators; get_indicator_history gives any card or row over time. Read-only, no account needed. Information, not investment advice.

as_of.description: Optional past date, YYYY-MM-DD, within the last 365 days: the dashboard as Jawz would have read it that day, from data published by then. Omit (or pass today) for today's dashboard.
